I have farmed this land for 30 years. I never went to school, but I know my fields. I watch what the good farmers in my village do, and I copy them. Last year my wheat got about 500 kg per mu, and my maize got about 550 kg per mu. That was okay, so I will do the same this year.

My wheat is already in the ground. Last autumn I ploughed deep and planted the big-ear improved wheat that my neighbor uses — the same seed every year because it works. At planting time I put down one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on every mu. Now that spring is here and the wheat is turning green, I will spread half a bag of urea on each mu. If the wheat looks a bit yellow when it shoots up, I will add another handful, because a bad harvest is a disaster and wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I will irrigate three times with my well pump: now at green-up, again at jointing, and once more when it flowers. The electricity bill for pumping is high, but dry wheat makes no grain. I will spray twice for bugs and mold.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I have only a few days before I must plant the maize. I will hire the rotary tiller man to go quick over the field, then plant hybrid maize seed — the yellow kind that everyone in the village buys. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, but I use a bit less urea than for wheat because maize is stronger and summer has some rain. I spread about 15 kg of urea per mu when the plants are knee-high. Two irrigations from the well should be enough in summer, but I will pump more if the sky stays dry for too long. Two sprays for insects and weeds.

I keep 2.4 mu near the house for stevia. My cousin's family grows it and the buyers pay good money for the leaves, so I copied them. I ploughed that plot fine and planted improved seedlings this spring. I give it half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, and a small handful of urea later when it grows taller. Stevia likes water, so I irrigate four times on that small plot — it is near the house so I can manage it. Two sprays for insects.

My son and daughter-in-law work in the county factory and send some money home, which helps. But fertilizer is expensive this year. I still buy the full amount for all my crops because I would rather spend a bit too much than risk losing yield. I think in bags: one bag of compound per mu for wheat and maize, half a bag for stevia, and urea on top. That is how I have always done it, and it feeds my family.
